name: Regulatory rulemaking
one_line: J-DEPTH placeholder template for the docket a rulemaking body keeps while making, amending, or revoking one binding instrument: a proposal that is itself a draft legal text, the analysis published to justify it, the comments received from parties the body does not control, the body's written response to those comments, and the made instrument that carries an effective date and an amend-or-revoke relationship to prior law. It is not activated by a regulator's name, by a docket-shaped or instrument-numbered token, by the words rule, regulation, consultation, or comment, or by possession of a published rule. Its discriminator is docket reciprocity — the same proposal reference appearing on an item the body issued AND on an item the body received, in the body's own custody — plus a stage chain that terminates in a made instrument.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: the government schema declares no field rows, so nothing below licenses a rulemaking fact. Every signal here decides ACTIVATION and GROUPING only. Unlike the schema default, an authority-side producer block is NOT required on every member: a rulemaking docket legitimately holds documents the body did not author.

DOCKET RECIPROCITY (the decisive signal, and the one the schema default cannot state): one exact proposal or docket reference printed both on an item the body ISSUED (a notice of proposed rulemaking, a draft instrument text, a published impact assessment) and on an item the body RECEIVED (a comment letter, a response form, a submission acknowledgement), with the received item held alongside the issued one rather than alongside its own drafting history

a proposal document whose body is DRAFT LEGAL TEXT — numbered regulations or sections with a citation-and-commencement provision, an interpretation provision, and amend-or-revoke wording pointing at a named prior instrument — rather than prose options or recommendations

a made instrument bearing the completion apparatus: a made or signed date distinct from the coming-into-force date, a signing officer or seal block of the rulemaking body, an instrument number, and an explicit statement of the enabling power it is made under

a response-to-comments structure: comment issues grouped and numbered, each with a summary of what was received and the body's stated reason for changing or not changing the draft, cross-referring to the same proposal reference
a comment index, docket manifest, or submission log listing received items by receipt number and date against one proposal reference — the record of receipt, held by the receiver

a stage chain across two DIFFERENT identifiers joined by an explicit cross-reference: the final instrument names the proposal or consultation it followed, or names the instrument it amends or revokes; rulemaking identifiers usually change at the moment of making, so a shared identifier alone will not assemble the chain
a regulatory impact assessment, cost-benefit analysis, or equivalent supporting analysis that is bound to a specific draft instrument by reference, not a standalone options appraisal
an accompanying explanatory memorandum or preamble that recites the proposal, the comment period, the volume or themes of response, and the changes made in consequence
a post-implementation review or sunset review naming the instrument by number and reporting whether the rule met its stated objective
an archive or export whose manifest lays out proposal, analysis, received comments, response, and instrument families under one proposal reference
needs_llm: whether a received document is a comment ON this proposal or an unrelated piece of correspondence that merely quotes the proposal reference
whether an item is held in the body's docket custody or is the regulated party's own retained copy of the same bytes
whether a proposal is a draft binding instrument or a policy option paper that has not reached instrument form
whether a permit-shaped document is a decision on one named applicant or a rule of general application wearing permit vocabulary (a general permit or class licence)
whether an internal draft is pre-decisional working material or the published version of the same text

whether a document belongs to the consultation mechanics (question set, response form, response-analysis summary) or to the instrument chain (draft text, bound impact assessment, response-to-comments, made instrument)

whether a body that is not obviously a public authority — a delegated standards body, a self-regulatory organisation, a professional regulator — is exercising a delegated rulemaking power or acting as a private association
never_alone: a regulator's or ministry's name in a filename, masthead, letterhead, or footer — the schema already excludes organisation names, and the regulated party's file bears the same masthead

a docket-shaped or instrument-shaped identifier token alone (agency-prefixed docket strings, a bare year-slash-number, a Federal Register document number) — the same shape serves case numbers, contract numbers, grant references, and citation strings
the words rule, rulemaking, regulation, regulatory, consultation, comment, notice, or instrument in a filename or heading
a comment letter with no evidence of receiver custody — the identical letter on the submitting firm's or campaign's drive is that party's advocacy record, not this docket
publication origin alone: a document downloaded from an official gazette, register, or legislation site is publication evidence, never custody evidence
draft-plus-legal-text shape alone — law-firm client alerts, trade-association briefings, and academic commentary reproduce draft regulation text verbatim
an impact assessment or cost-benefit analysis alone, which is equally at home in policy development, procurement business cases, and corporate compliance
absence of a producer block, absence of a signature, or absence of a made date is not proof that a document is pre-decisional or internal
a shared download session, a folder named for a regulator, or semantic similarity between two rule texts

work_types: notice of proposed rulemaking, consultation on a draft instrument, or advance notice of intent
draft instrument text or draft amendment text
supporting analysis: regulatory impact assessment, cost-benefit analysis, equality or environmental assessment bound to the draft
received comment, submission, or petition for rulemaking
comment index, docket manifest, or submission receipt log
response to comments, disposition table, or summary of consultation responses
final or made instrument, including the signing and commencement apparatus
explanatory memorandum, preamble, or statement of reasons accompanying the instrument
guidance, code, or compliance material issued alongside the instrument
commencement, transitional, savings, or corrections record
amendment or revocation instrument naming a prior instrument
post-implementation review, sunset review, or regulatory stock report
grouping_reasons: one docket, assembled by an exact proposal or docket reference that appears on BOTH an issued item and a received item in the same custody — the reciprocity is the anchor, because the reference alone appears on every regulated party's copy too

one stage chain across changed identifiers, joined only by an explicit cross-reference printed on the later document: the made instrument naming the proposal it followed, or naming the instrument it amends or revokes; without that printed link the two families stay separate candidates

one comment family, bounded by a receipt log or comment index that lists the members — mass-campaign duplicates of a single template letter form a duplicate family inside that boundary and must not be de-duplicated away, because the count of received identical letters is itself the record
one version family across drafts of the same instrument text, ordered by the stage endorsement or made date on the face of the document, not by filesystem timestamp
a supporting analysis joins the docket only through a printed binding reference to the draft instrument; a standalone appraisal with the same subject stays a separate candidate

template.why: Empty by contract: PR-6 leaves the government schema fieldless and a template cannot branch on undeclared fields. The prose recommendation, held for later adjudication, differs from the schema default in one respect that matters: the default says bounded proceeding first, then an exact reference, then work type; here the docket reference and the RULE STAGE are separate levels, because one docket spans proposal, comment, response, and instrument families that a user genuinely wants apart, and because the identifier changes at the moment of making so the docket level must be able to hold two references. A commenter's name must never become a dimension — that would publish a person-named branch out of received submissions. Time is not first: “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” Any later order stays editable because “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: Both publish a question set, receive named submissions, and produce a summary of what was received. Consultation owns the ENGAGEMENT EXERCISE and can exist with no instrument at the end of it — a service change, a budget, a strategy. This row owns the INSTRUMENT CHAIN and must terminate in, or aim at, a made instrument with an effective date and an amend-or-revoke relationship to prior law. Contested fixture: a consultation run on a draft instrument — the question set, the response form, and the response-analysis summary belong to public consultation; the draft instrument text, the impact assessment bound to it by reference, the response-to-comments annexed to the instrument, and the made instrument belong here. Received named submissions are held protected on both sides.

Impact assessments, options papers, briefings, and response analysis appear on both sides, often written by the same officials. Policy development terminates in a decision, a strategy, or a published policy; this row terminates in a legal instrument. Contested fixture: `Regulatory Impact Assessment - ENV-2026-0114 - final for publication.docx` — bound by printed reference to a draft instrument it accompanies, it is rulemaking evidence; the same assessment with no draft instrument anywhere and only options and recommendations around it is policy development. Neither side may conclude that the preferred option was adopted.

Reciprocal to the boundary that row already authored. A delegated instrument laid before a chamber generates documents on both sides. Contested fixture: `The Waste Carrier Registration (Amendment) Regulations 2026 - made - SI 2026 451.pdf` — the made instrument and its explanatory memorandum belong here, because they are the terminus of the making chain; the scrutiny committee's report on it, an annulment or objection motion, and the recorded division on that motion belong to the legislative record, because they are the chamber's own business about the instrument.

Both worlds are full of conditions, effective dates, and issuing-body signature blocks. Licensing applies an existing rule to one named applicant and produces a case with a holder; this row makes the rule of general application. Contested fixture: `General Permit GP-14 - discharges from small treatment works.pdf` — permit vocabulary but no named holder, eligibility stated by class, and a comment-period recital with a response annex, which makes it a rule wearing permit clothing and puts it here; the same body's `Permit PPC-2026-0442 - Acme Chemicals Ltd - variation decision.pdf` names a holder, an application, and a determination, and belongs to licensing.

A professional regulator both makes rules and decides cases about named registrants, with one masthead over both. A rulebook or code amendment consultation, its draft handbook text, and the made amendment instrument belong here; registration decisions, fitness-to-practise material, CPD audits, and any file organised around a named registrant belong to the professional regulator row. Contested fixture: `Consultation - proposed changes to the Code of Conduct - CP26-3.pdf` is rulemaking-shaped and comes here; `Fitness to Practise - Registrant 88213 - panel determination.pdf` never does, however similar the letterhead.

The same environmental body issues rules and runs enforcement against named operators. Contested fixture: `Comment 0231 - Acme Chemicals Ltd - ENV-2026-0114.pdf` — a comment on a proposal belongs here, keyed to the docket; `Enforcement Notice - Acme Chemicals Ltd - breach of condition 4.pdf` belongs to environmental regulation, keyed to the operator and the condition breached. The shared organisation name decides nothing on either side.

The regulated firm keeps the same NPRM PDF, the same draft instrument, and its own comment letter. The deciding evidence is custody direction: received-and-logged by the body versus drafted-and-approved by the firm. Contested fixture: `Consultation response - FINAL - approved by GC - v7.docx` — with an internal version family, a legal-review markup, and an approval thread, it is the firm's regulatory-affairs record; the same text arriving with a receipt stamp and a receipt number in the body's comment index is this row's member. Reciprocally, a copy of a made instrument on the firm's drive is the firm's compliance reference, not a docket member.

A campaign organisation drafts a template comment, mobilises supporters, and files thousands of near-identical responses. The campaign's own copy, its supporter-mobilisation material, its action alerts, and its response tracker are advocacy records. Contested fixture: the mass-campaign duplicate letter — inside the body's comment index it is a member of this docket's duplicate family and its count is part of the record; on the campaign's drive beside its mobilisation assets it is the campaign's. Neither side may treat volume as evidence of anything beyond receipt.

A firm advising on or challenging a rule holds the proposal, the comments, the instrument, and its own analysis. This row requires the making body's custody; the practitioner side requires representation evidence tying the material to a client matter. Contested fixture: a petition or claim for judicial review of `SI 2026 451` — the petition, the pleadings, and counsel's analysis are matter-file material; a petition FOR rulemaking, received and logged by the body against a docket, is this row's member.

falls_through_to.when: a published rule, notice, gazette extract, consultation document, or guidance is held for reading or reference with no docket custody and no proposal-side sibling
falls_through_to.design_cite: Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.

falls_through_to.when: a received named submission, a submitter contact block, a comment index carrying withhold flags, a pre-publication internal draft, or a hearing recording of named speakers has no safe accepted docket group
falls_through_to.design_cite: Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.

falls_through_to.when: a made instrument, explanatory memorandum, or issued guidance has durable standalone value but no assembled docket around it
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.when: the document is rulemaking-shaped but the custody direction, the body's public status, or the proposal-versus-policy question cannot be settled safely
falls_through_to.design_cite: Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.

falls_through_to.when: an encrypted docket archive, a damaged export, or an inaccessible case-system binary yields nothing beyond metadata
falls_through_to.design_cite: Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.

falls_through_to.when: a positively evidenced screen capture of a docket portal or gazette page yields no accepted docket group by OCR
falls_through_to.design_cite: Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.

role_split.note: Same entity type on both sides of one comment: the body that received it and the party that sent it. The government schema declares no field rows, so no role key can be written; the split is recorded as a custody-direction recognition rule until PR-6 is lifted.

sensitivity_why: A rulemaking docket is deliberately public in part and strictly not public in part, and the two live in the same folder. Received submissions carry named individuals, contact blocks, small-business identities, and sometimes withhold-my-details requests; comment indexes carry redaction and publication-status columns; pre-publication drafts, draft response-to-comments, and internal reviewer names are pre-decisional and market-sensitive before the instrument is made. That a rule is published does not lower the posture of the docket around it. The design requires: “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.” Only none and potentially_sensitive exist in this phase; P7 owns handling classes, publication decisions, and any embargo policy.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: the seam against government.public-consultation is the thinnest boundary in this domain, because a consultation on a draft instrument produces documents both rows can justify holding. This node proposes engagement-exercise versus instrument-chain, splitting one real consultation packet across two rows. The alternatives are (a) fold consultation into rulemaking wherever a draft instrument exists, leaving consultation only non-instrument engagement, (b) fold rulemaking's comment stage into consultation, leaving this row only proposal, analysis, and instrument, or (c) keep the proposed split and accept the packet is divided. R1c should decide reciprocally with the public-consultation row rather than let each side assume it wins.
